methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: McLean data center power-focused startup to be acquired for $232.28M
signals.signal_reading: A $232M acquisition of a McLean data center infrastructure startup signals deepening concentration of AI-enabling capital infrastructure in NoVA, reinforcing the region's gravitational pull for technical talent and specialized expertise that remains geographically bounded.

signals.title: Anthropic unveils new framework allowing AI agents to operate physical devices
signals.signal_reading: Anthropic's framework for AI-operated physical devices creates potential for deep AI integration in Virginia's manufacturing sectors, but adoption will likely concentrate in regions with existing advanced manufacturing and technical workforce capacity rather than distributing broadly.

signals.title: Parents call for less screen time, more intentional use of technology in schools
signals.signal_reading: Parental pushback against technology in Southwest/Southside schools signals resistance to even shallow digital adoption in rural regions, potentially constraining the pipeline for future AI fluency precisely where intervention is most needed to prevent concentration.

signals.title: Craig County supervisor: Virginia’s broken school funding formula is hitting rural families the hardest
signals.signal_reading: Broken school funding formulas in rural Craig County directly undermine the educational infrastructure necessary for distributed AI capability building, systematically disadvantaging regions that lack the tax base to self-fund technology workforce development.

signals.title: New proposal from grid operator PJM would require data centers to bring their own power
signals.signal_reading: PJM's 'bring your own power' requirement for data centers may reinforce concentration by favoring well-capitalized NoVA developments over potential distributed data infrastructure, as only metro areas can marshal the resources for integrated power solutions.
